title: Fix inert status live-region: announcement text is overwritten post-boot
outcome: The status cell's aria-live=polite region actually announces save/export/recovery messages: post-boot writes keep the live-region element stable (message text changes in place) so sighted users see 'Saved...'/'PDF exported...' and screen readers announce them, with the doc-size label moving to its own non-live element.
before: Batch critic finding 2026-08-28 (VIRO-0016 post-merge review, F8 follow-up): #stat-engine's aria-live=polite is inert after boot because src/chrome/desk.ts:1853 overwrites the element with the doc-size label whenever engines are up, so 'Saved...'/'PDF exported...' never display for sighted or screen-reader users (probe read 'Doc: 33.2M/33.2M' immediately after Ctrl+S). The a11y builder disclosed this honestly as out of VIRO-0016's lease.
after: Status messages render and are announced; doc-size label lives elsewhere; desk.ts:1853 no longer clobbers the live region; covered by a test asserting the live element survives a status write after boot.
acceptance: After engines boot, a save action renders 'Saved...' (or current truthful wording) in the status cell AND the aria-live element remains the same node announcing it (test asserts node identity + text).
Doc-size label renders in its own element; no clobbering of the live region (desk.ts:1853 path fixed).
VIRO-0016's a11y suite stays green; no visual drift beyond the corrected status content.
npx tsc --noEmit, new test, npm run test:chrome and npm run build pass.
evidence: Screenshot of visible status message post-save

builder.notes: Builder zcode-status-pc1 (pc-cloud1), branch agent/viro-0148/zcode-gov-audit-pc1 based on fc96f44 (includes 0016 a11y + 0017 polish chrome; composed, not regressed). Before-state re-confirmed: index.html #stat-engine was the ONLY aria-live=polite cell and desk.ts:1853 wrote docSizeLabel(page,...) into it whenever app.engines was set, clobbering every post-boot app.status message (save/export/recovery) on the next render; screen readers and sighted users both lost the message. Fix (2 product files, inside lease): (1) index.html adds a dedicated non-live <span class="stat" id="stat-docsize" hidden> slot before the live cell; #stat-engine keeps aria-live=polite and the grow slot as the ONE status channel; (2) desk.ts render now writes app.status into #stat-engine textContent IN PLACE behind a change guard (no element replacement, no innerHTML swap; the guard also stops re-render churn from rewriting identical text into the live node, which screen readers can re-announce), and renders docSizeLabel into #stat-docsize only while app.engines is up — the slot stays hidden and empty during boot (truthful: no document to measure yet). Regression suite tests/a11y-status-live.spec.ts: (T1) pins the exact pre-save #stat-engine element in the page, presses Ctrl+S, asserts 'Saved … to Projects' text AND that the announcing node IS the pinned node (same reference, isConnected, aria-live=polite preserved) — node identity + text as frozen; (T2) proves the announcement survives later render churn (zoom commands re-run the render path that used to clobber it) and that the Doc: readout sits in #stat-docsize which carries NO aria-live attribute; (T3) post-boot slot/region content contract + committed statusbar screenshot. Bite check: with the fix git-stashed (pre-fix desk.ts+index.html) the same suite FAILS 3/3; with the fix it PASSES 3/3 — the guard is real, not vacuous. Evidence shots committed under tests/a11y-status-shots/ (statusbar-after-save.png reads: Untitled | Zoom 21% | 2480 x 3508 px | 300 ppi | RGB/8 | Doc: 33.2M/33.2M | Saved "Untitled" to Projects — doc-size in its own cell, truthful message in the live region, matching the critic probe's 33.2M/33.2M numbers). tests/a11y-status-playwright.config.ts is the seat-local gate runner on the assigned port 5211 (0017 seat-port pattern; reuseExistingServer:false; workers:1 after observing default 2 workers make two SwiftShader Chromium instances contend and randomly miss the 90s bootReady gate across ALL suites).
